key_symbols.name: Geometry
key_symbols.role: Eight-field struct reed is told its coordinates through once at construction; never derives or validates itself.

key_symbols.name: reedcli.attachCmd
key_symbols.role: Reads the operator's own terminal size via golang.org/x/term.GetSize(stdout fd) before handing stdio to tmux, and passes cols/rows into Engine.AttachArgv.

key_symbols.name: Engine.AttachArgv
key_symbols.role: Builds the attach argv; on a usable client size, chains a select-layout computed from that client's told box onto the attach-session command so the new client's geometry lands verbatim instead of being live-queried.

key_symbols.name: Engine.readWindowSizeLatestLocked / readStatusRowsLocked
key_symbols.role: Read back tmux's effective window-size/status option values and compare them against the expected pinned values ("latest"/off); a mismatch suppresses the geometry chain (errAttachChainSuppressed), falling back to the bare attach argv.

key_symbols.name: Engine.liveBoxLocked
key_symbols.role: Queries tmux's current live window size (display-message) and returns it as a render.Box, with a fallback to configured Width/Height on error; this is the freshly-read size used for in-session (non-attach) layout recompute.

key_symbols.name: Engine.planLayout
key_symbols.role: Pure function mapping the persisted strand table plus a supplied box into a tmux window_layout string; never queries tmux itself, so its caller decides whether the box is live-queried or client-told.

key_symbols.name: Engine.applyLayoutLocked
key_symbols.role: Applies the computed layout via tmux select-layout using e.liveBoxLocked()'s freshly-queried live window size as the box passed to planLayout — this is how a mid-session resize is reconciled: every mutating op recomputes the layout against the currently-live window size rather than a stored one.

key_symbols.name: reconcileApplyPersistLocked
key_symbols.role: Shared reconcile-then-apply-then-persist tail every public engine op (add/update/remove/resume) runs, which is what causes geometry to be re-derived on every session-mutating action, including resume/reattach-adjacent flows.

key_symbols.name: planReconcile / reconcileLocked
key_symbols.role: Reconciles the persisted strand/pane table against tmux's live pane list before layout is computed; strictly about pane liveness, not window geometry itself.

summary: Terminal geometry is never persisted as a stored value reed diffs against later; instead there are two distinct read points that feed the same pure planLayout function. During an ordinary session mutation (add/remove/update/resume), applyLayoutLocked (apply.go) freshly queries tmux's actual live window size via liveBoxLocked (windowsize.go, a display-message round trip, falling back to the configured Width/Height on error) and recomputes the window_layout string against that live box every single time — so a resize between operations is 'reconciled' simply by always re-deriving layout from the current live size rather than trusting a stale one, and the code explicitly notes this must be the live box (not the configured one) because select-layout silently rescales proportionally when the layout string's dimensions disagree with the real window. On (re)attach, reedcli/attach.go instead reads the *attaching client's own* terminal size via golang.org/x/term.GetSize and passes cols/rows into Engine.AttachArgv (attach.go), which — after pinning 'status off'/'window-size latest' and reading those pins back to confirm they took effect — computes a layout from the client's told box and chains a select-layout onto the attach-session tmux argv itself, timed to run only once the client has actually attached (so tmux's own auto-rescale on attach can't clobber the planned string first, per the attachgeometry_integration_test.go regression this guards). The 'compare previously-known vs freshly-read and react to a difference' step is this option-readback check (readWindowSizeLatestLocked/readStatusRowsLocked comparing the actual tmux option values against the pinned expectation) plus the live-pane-count/placed-strand guards; any mismatch triggers errAttachChainSuppressed and AttachArgv degrades to the bare, unchained attach-session argv rather than ever returning an error, since attach must remain an unconditional escape hatch.
open_questions: The task's phrase 'previously-known geometry compared against a freshly-read one' does not map to a literal stored-old-box vs new-box diff anywhere in these two packages — the design instead always fully recomputes from whichever box source (live query vs client-told) is authoritative for that code path. I've treated the closest analogues (the option-pin readback checks, and live-box-vs-stale-configured-box) as the intended reconciliation point, but a different reading of 'reconciliation' may exist elsewhere in a file I didn't need to open.
